target.title: fix(ui): preserve sidebar session list on Gateway disconnect
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves When the Gateway disconnects, `app-sidebar.ts` immediately clears the sidebar session list via two code paths: 1. `updateGatewayClient()` unconditionally resets `sessionRowsByAgent` and `sessionCreatedOrder` on every client change 2. `updateSessions()` unconditionally overwrites `sessionsResult` with `null` pushed by the subscription on disconnect Users see their entire sidebar session list disappear, with no indication that the data will come back after reconnect. ## Why This Change Was Made Three targeted fixes: 1. **`updateSessions`**: Guard `sessionsResult` overwrite — only update when `snapshot.result !== null`, so the subscription cannot wipe the list on disconnect. 2. **`updateGatewayClient`**: Replace the per-client-change reset with a permanent `sidebarEverConnected` flag. The session caches are cleared exactly once — on the very first connection. Disconnect/reconnect cycles never reset them. 3. The sessions subscription (`context.sessions.subscribe`) remains the sole mechanism for refreshing rows when Gateway reconnects. ## Evidence **Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout, Node v24.13.1, PR head. ### Before Fix (current main) **Observed:** Gateway disconnect wipes the sidebar session list instantly. Users see a blank sidebar with no sessions and no explanation. The session list only returns after a full page refresh or after the sessions subscription eventually fires on reconnect. ### After Fix (PR head) **Observed:** Gateway disconnect does not clear the sidebar. Sessions remain visible throughout the disconnect window. The header banner correctly indicates the connection state. When Gateway reconnects, the sessions subscription automatically refreshes the list with current data. ## Root Cause Two code paths in `app-sidebar.ts` unconditionally discard session data on Gateway state changes: - `updateGatewayClient()` (line 276): `this.sessionRowsByAgent = {}; this.sessionCreatedOrder.clear();` fires on every `client` reference change — disconnect, reconnect, or first connect. - `updateSessions()` (line 253): `this.sessionsResult = snapshot.result;` overwrites the cached result with `null` when the subscription fires during disconnect. Both paths assume the data is stale on any change, but during a transient Gateway disconnect/reconnect cycle, the last-known data is still valid and should remain visible until the subscription delivers fresh data.
